active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06), driven primarily by a defect in the billing calculation/import-validation step that produces incorrect bills even when the underlying meter read was correctly recorded as ACTUAL: disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) reads (E-01), ruling out estimate-substitution (AMI or field read gaps) as the primary driver. Route completion for manual-read accounts fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026, affecting 9200 accounts, confirming a real field read-delivery shortfall during the dispute-surge window. However, since E-01 showed disputed bills are dominated by ACTUAL (not ESTIMATED) reads, this gap can at most be a partial/secondary contributor to the dispute surge rather than its primary cause.

release_summary.summary: The investigated problem was a doubling of billing dispute tickets from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), per CRM data (E-06). The requester's framing (an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills, CL-01) was ruled out because response times were already within SLA (E-05). Evidence traced one bucket of disputes - estimated-read bills - to a billing-import rule, BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month history without unit scaling (E-13). Firmware v4.2 meters report readings in 0.1 m3 sub-units instead of whole m3 (E-14), so legitimate high-usage reads are misclassified and rejected at import: 1184 of 1240 disputed estimated-read bills were rejected as high-consumption, matching exactly 1184 identified firmware-v4.2 accounts (E-12, E-15, E-16). Field-staffing/route-completion explanations (E-02/E-07) were invalidated for this bucket once E-12 showed the import mechanism was responsible instead. Tariff change was ruled out (E-03, E-04). However, most disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, read type (E-01), and whether BV-17 explains that larger group remains unconfirmed, tracked as open VOB-U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the released scope is confined to diagnostic/monitoring work (verifying the firmware/unit-scaling defect, monitoring dispute-volume trend) because the confirmed BV-17/firmware mechanism for the estimated-read bucket is solid evidence worth delivering now, while causal confirmation for the ACTUAL-read majority and the actual rule fix are not yet done. No bill corrections or rule changes were made or authorized; billing-config (DA-RULES) is read-only to this role, and bill writes require manual Billing Operations action under K-BILLWRITE, so affected accounts remain uncorrected pending further work.

output.root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06), with onset coinciding with billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01), which compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13). symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06).

Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout June 2026) report reads in 0.1 m3 sub-units versus whole m3 used by older firmware/history (E-14).
The majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, read type, a magnitude not yet traced to the confirmed import-rejection mechanism (E-01).
causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 meters, rolled out June 2026, report register reads in 0.1 m3 sub-units while older firmware and the historical baseline use whole m3 (E-14).
Billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling applied (E-13).
For v4.2-metered accounts this unscaled comparison inflates apparent consumption roughly 10x, triggering the high-consumption anomaly check.
1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills were rejected at billing import under REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 more had no AMI read received at all (E-12).
Rejected or missing reads trigger estimate substitution, producing bills customers perceive as wrong and dispute.
Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month to ~1200-1260/month starting August 2026, matching BV-17's deployment date (E-06, E-13).

However, most disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, read type (E-01), and whether BV-17 explains that larger group remains unconfirmed, tracked as open VOB-U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the released scope is confined to diagnostic/monitoring work (verifying the firmware/unit-scaling defect, monitoring dispute-volume trend) because the confirmed BV-17/firmware mechanism for the estimated-read bucket is solid evidence worth delivering now, while causal confirmation for the ACTUAL-read majority and the actual rule fix are not yet done.
